rule.description: A contiguous run of at least three adjacent named parameters recurs, with the same names in the same order, in at least three distinct free-function signatures of one crate: a cohesive data group travels through signatures lacking a named owner type.
rule.implementation: Custom Dylint late-lint pass (`data_clumps` library embedded in smell_check.sh) over a workspace-wide cargo check; methods and trait-impl signatures are out of scope (they already hang off an owner type); non-binding parameter patterns break a run; thresholds: min window 3 parameters, min carriers 3 signatures, max window 8.

checks.description: Server-side session material (certificate, private key, optional client-CA) enumerated as the adjacent parameters cert, key, ca across free functions of the TLS network layer.
checks.detected_relation: free function signature -> recurring [cert,key,ca] parameter run shared across sibling free-function signatures of the same crate
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The three values are exactly what building one server-side TLS session needs; the free functions of each generation re-enumerate them layer by layer (configuration build, stream accept, per-connection hand-off) because no owner type names the bundle.

checks.description: Client-side session material (optional identity certificate and key, optional server CA) enumerated as the adjacent parameters id_cert, id_key, server_ca across free functions of the TLS network layer.
checks.detected_relation: free function signature -> recurring [id_cert,id_key,server_ca] parameter run shared across sibling free-function signatures of the same crate
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The identity pair and the trust anchor form the client side of one TLS decision; the free functions re-enumerate them at every stage (configuration build, connector construction, connect step, config bootstrap) instead of passing one named session-owner value.
